Annotate a data frame

Source: R/annotate.R
laya_annotate.Rd

Asks the same questions about every row of a data frame and adds the answers as new columns, one or more per question:

Usage

laya_annotate(
  data,
  questions,
  state,
  engine = laya_default_engine(),
  ...,
  prefix = "",
  confidence = TRUE,
  answer_confidence = FALSE,
  probabilities = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble. A tibble stays a tibble.

questions

A question set (laya_questions(), a preset, or anything as_laya_questions() accepts).

state

The name or names of the column(s) the model reads, as strings ("text", c("subject", "body")), not bare names. With one column, its text is the state as is. With several, each row becomes a structured state such as {"subject": ..., "body": ...}, which keeps the field names as context for the model.

engine

A laya_engine(). Defaults to laya_default_engine().

...

Passed to laya_predict_batch(): min_confidence, lang, batch_size, chunk_size, progress and the token budgets.

prefix

A prefix for the new column names, for example "laya_".

confidence

Add a <id>_confidence column per question?

answer_confidence

Add a <id>_answer_confidence column per question: the confidence in the answer given, which min_confidence compares with its threshold. For a choice question it is the chosen option's probability.

probabilities

Add a <id>_probabilities list-column per question, holding each option's probability as a named numeric vector?

Value

data with the new columns. Rows whose state columns are all missing get NA answers instead of a prediction.

Details

  • a choice question gives a factor whose levels are the options, in order;

  • a score question gives the expected level (a number from 0 to the number of levels minus one);

  • a yes/no question gives the probability that the statement is true.

With confidence = TRUE each answer also gets a <id>_confidence column. With min_confidence (passed in ...), each gated answer also gets a logical <id>_abstained column. The answer is kept either way; filter on the column to drop low-confidence answers. The gate compares the threshold with each answer's answer_confidence (for a choice question, the chosen option's probability), which can differ from the <id>_confidence column; answer_confidence = TRUE adds it as a <id>_answer_confidence column.

See also

laya_predict_batch() for the full results.

Examples

if (laya_model_available()) {
  tickets <- data.frame(
    subject = c("Duplicate charge", "App crashes on login"),
    body = c("We were billed twice. Refund it or we cancel.", "Since the update I can't log in.")
  )
  qs <- laya_questions(
    department = laya_choice("Which department should handle this?",
                             billing = "invoices, refunds", technical = "bugs, outages"),
    churn_risk = laya_noul("Does the customer threaten to cancel?")
  )
  laya_annotate(tickets, qs, state = c("subject", "body"))
}
